parsed.explanation: Entry documents are the sharpest exposure: the Feb 2025 visa cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, with a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; the X-marker is barred and markers must match assigned sex at birth (SCOTUS allowed this Nov 2025); travellers report passports blocked/confiscated and eight foreign governments issued advisories. Facilities: federal single-sex exclusion plus the division's birth-certificate school/college designation law (no enforcement mechanism, no documented arrests). Custody: corrections-bureau conversion-therapy policy and immigration-detention abuse of trans detainees (beatings, sexual abuse) are documented if discovery leads to detention.

entry_documents.exposure: X-marker barred; markers must match assigned sex at birth; discrepancy or 'reasonable doubt' triggers visa refusal, with fraud/lifetime-ineligibility exposure; travellers report passports blocked or confiscated, some stranded abroad; foreign advisories issued.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires all four elements, has limited waivers, and is never automatic; litigation pending; old X passports valid to expiration.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch → secondary screening → refusal → possible immigration custody, where trans-detainee abuse is documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies (hair cutting, hormone removal) for trans inmates; trans immigration detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Several executive orders blocked or enjoined; some custody reforms were rescinded but remedies untested for visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility-law or document encounters can escalate into these custody systems; visitor status offers no shield documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; division law (Feb 2025) requires birth-certificate-based designation in all public and private schools/colleges; nationally 21+ units restrict facilities, 4 criminalize in some circumstances; one trans student arrested elsewhere.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division facility law has no enforcement mechanism and no documented arrest; single-occupancy restrooms exempt; municipal public-accommodation ordinances in 33 cities/counties.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Criminal-trespass regimes elsewhere heighten friction; division exposure is institutional refusal rather than arrest.

care_services.exposure: Division care/sports act (blockers, hormones, surgery for under-18s; sports ban) has been enjoined and re-enjoined; adult replacement rules withdrawn; federal proposals bar insurance coverage for under-18s — direct exposure for a visiting minor.
care_services.protection: Appeals court re-enjoined the act March 2025; proposed perpetual-counselling adult rules were dropped and are not in force.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor's care can become an enforcement or investigation subject under Jan 2025 orders on schools.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders frame care as 'mutilation,' direct law-enforcement investigation of 'gender ideology'; counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups; DOJ reward memo lists 'radical gender ideology' among extremist viewpoints; 2025 poll shows 66% backing birth-sex markers.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The reward criterion never uses 'radical gender ideology'; strategy states counterterrorism powers won't target mere disagreement; courts have enjoined several orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Elevates discovery probability and official hostility during any document or police encounter.

minors_guardians.exposure: Jan 2025 order directs criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating a minor's social transition; division law forces outing of LGBTQ students to parents (Jan 2025); care ban litigation unresolved; facility designation binds schools.
minors_guardians.protection: Facility law unenforced; care act re-enjoined March 2025; municipal conversion-therapy bans for minors in several cities.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting minor presenting incongruently with documents risks school-style disclosure norms bleeding into official encounters.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity, but only 23 units include gender identity in bias statutes; no division-specific incident record; social climate shows majority support for birth-sex document rules.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime coverage; employment discrimination prohibited nationally (2020 ruling) and by division executive order; 33 local non-discrimination ordinances.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin local incident data means recourse exists on paper but enforcement against visitors is undocumented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport challenge unresolved after SCOTUS allowed restrictions; division marker-rule text and effective date unsourced; tier methodology unclear; enforcement of facility designation unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Multiple orders blocked or enjoined; legal-aid FAQ running; district court invalidated marker-change bar; litigation is active and sometimes succeeds.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Partial judicial pushback mitigates paper exposure but has not reversed the operative document regime travellers face.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.35-A, this jurisdiction imposes a routine traveller-facing exclusion regime keyed to trans status with near-useless appeals. It rates higher because refusals here are discretionary, waiver-litigated and jurisdiction-dependent rather than a universal unpublished register, and no criminal penalty attaches locally.

Worse than 0.55-B: that anchor's harm is administrative delay and discretionary refusal; here refusal carries possible lifetime ineligibility, custody systems documentedly abuse trans detainees, and facility exclusion is statutorily mandated. Longer remedies do not offset severity.

Well below 0.75-C, which shows trained border staff, tribunal appeal and brief detention ending in release. Here the document regime is deliberately restrictive and validated at the top court, with custody-abuse reports contradicting the protective picture.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime's core exposure is universal document friction: a trans visitor cannot make federal (or, since Aug 2026, division) markers match presentation, so discovery at any check is close to unavoidable, and discovery feeds a refusal regime with fraud/lifetime-ineligibility tail risk and documented abuse inside immigration custody. Facility exclusion is real but, in this division, an unenforced institutional rule rather than a criminal one; the care/sports act is enjoined. Counterweight: functioning federal employment and hate-crime protections, 33 local non-discrimination ordinances, marriage recognition, active litigation that has blocked several orders, and no trans-specific criminal offence. Majority public support for birth-sex markers plus official threat-framing keeps social exposure elevated. Net: exclusion, humiliation, service denial and conditional detention risk, not imprisonment as the ordinary outcome — Elevated Risk.
